title: Algorithms and Boolean Logic (KS4 Computer Science)
subject: Computer Science
strapline: Step-by-step problem solving and the logic gates behind it.
facts: An algorithm is a precise, step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or complete a task.
Algorithms can be shown as pseudocode or as a flowchart.
Decomposition means breaking a problem into smaller, manageable parts; abstraction means removing unnecessary detail.
Two key searching algorithms: linear search (check each item in turn) and binary search (repeatedly halve a sorted list).
Common sorting algorithms include bubble sort and merge sort.
The three basic logic gates are AND, OR and NOT.
AND outputs 1 only if both inputs are 1; OR outputs 1 if either input is 1; NOT inverts the input.

quick_quiz.a: a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem

quick_quiz.q: Which search requires the list to be sorted first?
When does an AND gate output 1?

teacher_tips: Trace algorithms by hand with a data table before coding them.
Binary search needs a sorted list — a common exam trap.
Build truth tables for each gate to embed the logic.
